audits.title: 247 BENCHMARKING STROKE SERVICES TO INFORM A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INIAITIVE
audits.standard: Irish National Audit of Stroke 2019, 6th SSNAP Annual Report and AHA 2013 indicators
audits.setting: University Hospital Limerick (university teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: Thrombolysis 10%; median door to needle 60 minutes; stroke unit admission 78.5%; swallow assessment 81.1%; inpatient mortality 10.5%; thrombectomy 1.9%; median door to imaging 104 minutes; mood screening 11.5%; median stay 12 days.

audits.intervention: Ongoing PDSA quality improvement with annual audit (planned)
audits.other_findings: Thrombectomy, length of stay, time to imaging and mood screening were the areas for improvement.
audits.citation: Loughlin E, Gannon E, Coughlan A, Cunningham N, Paulose S, O'Brien I, et al.. 247 BENCHMARKING STROKE SERVICES TO INFORM A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INIAITIVE. Age and Ageing. 2021;50(Supplement_3):ii9-ii41. doi:10.1093/ageing/afab219.247.

audits.title: The national sentinel audit for stroke: a tool for raising standards of care.
audits.standard: Intercollegiate Stroke Audit
audits.setting: 197 trusts in England, Wales and Northern Ireland

cycle1.result: Swallow screening 55%, cognitive testing 23%, visual field examination 44%; MDT rehabilitation goals 55%; GP contact within 3 days of discharge 41%; 64% of trusts had a stroke physician and 50% a stroke team.

audits.other_findings: Best compliance for the 18% of patients who spent at least 50% of their stay on a stroke unit.
audits.citation: Rudd AG, Irwin P, Rutledge Z, Lowe D, Wade D, Morris R, et al.. The national sentinel audit for stroke: a tool for raising standards of care. J R Coll Physicians Lond. 1999;33(5):460-464. doi:10.1016/s0035-8819(25)01663-0. PMID: 10624664.

audits.title: National stroke audit: a tool for change?
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians Intercollegiate Working Party stroke audit standards
audits.setting: 157 trusts in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (National Sentinel Audit of Stroke)

cycle1.result: 19% of patients managed on stroke units.

audits.intervention: Active national dissemination strategy of audit results.

cycle2.result: Stroke unit management rose to 26%; formal cognitive assessment 41%, weighed 46%, physiotherapy assessment within 72 h 67%, mood plan 24%, carers' needs assessed 36%.

audits.other_findings: Many standards remained poor despite improvement on both stroke units and general wards.
audits.citation: Rudd AG, Lowe D, Irwin P, Rutledge Z, Pearson M, Intercollegiate Stroke Working Party. National stroke audit: a tool for change?. Qual Health Care. 2001;10(3):141-151. doi:10.1136/qhc.0100141... PMID: 11533421.

audits.title: Evaluation of stroke management in an Irish university teaching hospital: the Royal College of Physicians stroke audit package.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians stroke audit package (13 key areas)
audits.setting: Beaumont Hospital, Dublin, university teaching hospital

cycle1.result: CT and carotid Dopplers documented in 93%; power 87%, sensation 70%, eye movements 63%, but cognition 3%, visual fields 13%, gait 7%, incontinence 1% and swallowing 0%.

audits.other_findings: Diagnostic formulation and acute management plan documented in under half; secondary prevention in two-thirds.

audits.title: Audit of stroke care at the Institute of Neurology, National Hospital of Sri Lanka, 1994-1997.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians of London stroke audit package (60 audit items across 13 aspects of care)
audits.setting: Institute of Neurology, National Hospital of Sri Lanka, Colombo

cycle1.result: Care was 'very good' for 11 (18.3%), 'good' for 9 (15%), 'average' for 5 (8.3%), 'poor' for 9 (15%) and 'very poor' for 26 (43.3%) of the 60 audit items.

audits.other_findings: Rehabilitation-oriented neurological assessment, secondary prevention, rehabilitation planning and discharge planning were especially deficient.
audits.citation: Ranawaka UK, Fernando MA, Gunasekera TG, Senanayake BS, Gunawardena DR, Wijesekera JC, et al.. Audit of stroke care at the Institute of Neurology, National Hospital of Sri Lanka, 1994-1997. Ceylon Med J. 2002;47(3):86-88. doi:10.4038/cmj.v47i3.3435. PMID: 12449773.

audits.title: Stroke audit.
audits.standard: Clinical documentation of key stroke assessments

cycle1.result: Documentation: Barthel 0%, depression 0%, mental score 1.0%, vision 10.0%, continence 39.6%, admission function 37.6%, dysphagia 52.5%.

audits.title: Quality of stroke care within a hospital: effects of a mobile stroke service.
audits.standard: SCOPES stroke care quality indicators, with localised stroke units as the gold standard
audits.setting: 260-bed hospital in Melbourne

cycle1.result: Historical controls before the mobile stroke service: severe complications 24%; median length of stay 18.5 days; 9% independent at discharge.

cycle2.result: Significant improvements in DVT prophylaxis, incontinence management, premorbid function documentation, frequent neurological observations and early occupational therapy; severe complications 9% (P = 0.004); median stay 12.0 days (P = 0.003); 32% independent at discharge.

audits.other_findings: MSS results were also compared with stroke units in SCOPES.
audits.citation: van der Walt A, Gilligan AK, Cadilhac DA, Brodtmann AG, Pearce DC, Donnan GA. Quality of stroke care within a hospital: effects of a mobile stroke service. Med J Aust. 2005;182(4):160-163. doi:10.5694/j.1326-5377.2005.tb06645.x. PMID: 15720170.

audits.title: Guideline recommendations for the management of patients admitted with acute stroke: implications of a local audit.
audits.standard: New Zealand guideline for management of stroke
audits.setting: Hawke's Bay Hospital

cycle1.result: Brain imaging 100% (86% within 48 hours); aspirin or documented contraindication within 48 hours 62%; swallowing and mobility assessment within 48 hours 88%; driving advice documented in only 19%.

audits.other_findings: 8 patients (16%) were wrongly coded as stroke; those not admitted directly to the stroke unit (38%) were less likely to receive recommended care.
audits.citation: Gommans J, Sye D, MacDonald A. Guideline recommendations for the management of patients admitted with acute stroke: implications of a local audit. N Z Med J. 2005;118(1214):U1435. PMID: 15886730.

audits.title: Improving clinical practice in stroke through audit: results of three rounds of National Stroke Audit.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians national stroke audit process standards
audits.setting: Trusts in England, Wales and Northern Ireland taking part in all three rounds of the National Stroke Audit

cycle1.result: 48% of hospitals had a stroke unit; 17% of patients spent most of their stay on a stroke unit.

audits.intervention: Repeated national audit rounds (specific changes not reported)

cycle2.result: 77% of hospitals had a stroke unit; 29% spent most of their stay on a stroke unit; process standards showed no further median gain after 1999 (median change 0%).

audits.other_findings: In 1999 (4841 cases) process standards improved by a median 9%; 7- and 30-day mortality fell by 3% and 5%; care was better on stroke units.
audits.citation: Irwin P, Hoffman A, Lowe D, Pearson M, Rudd AG. Improving clinical practice in stroke through audit: results of three rounds of National Stroke Audit. J Eval Clin Pract. 2005;11(4):306-314. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2753.2005.00529.x. PMID: 16011643.

audits.title: Data feedback for quality improvement of stroke care: CAPTURE Stroke experience.
audits.standard: Stroke quality indicators (DVT prophylaxis, dysphagia screening, antithrombotics, warfarin for AF, lipid screening, smoking counselling)
audits.setting: 13 hospitals (CAPTURE Stroke)

cycle1.result: Baseline chart audit of quality indicators (figures not given).

audits.intervention: Feedback of baseline audit results to 7 of 13 hospitals; 6 had chart audit only.

cycle2.result: Difference in mean change, feedback vs no feedback: lipid screening 19.93 (90% CI 2.99 to 36.86); DVT prophylaxis 8.46; smoking counselling 17.47; warfarin for AF 44.73 (not significant).

audits.other_findings: Most differences were not statistically significant.
audits.citation: Pandey DK, Cursio JF, CAPTURE Stroke Investigators. Data feedback for quality improvement of stroke care: CAPTURE Stroke experience. Am J Prev Med. 2006;31(6 Suppl 2):S224-9. doi:10.1016/j.amepre.2006.08.006. PMID: 17178307.

audits.title: An audit of the impact of implementation of a stroke care pathway in an acute teaching hospital.
audits.standard: UK National Stroke Audit 2002 benchmarks
audits.setting: Galway Regional Hospital, acute teaching hospital

cycle1.result: Management of stroke patients lacked organised and specialised care.

audits.intervention: Introduction of a stroke care pathway for general medical teams

cycle2.result: Marked deficits persisted, including delays in brain imaging and aspirin administration, assessment of acute parameters and interdisciplinary care.

audits.other_findings: Authors recommend a stroke unit with a consultant-led multidisciplinary team.

audits.title: Quality of in-hospital stroke care according to evidence-based performance measures: results from the first audit of stroke, Catalonia, Spain.
audits.standard: 13 evidence-based performance measures of in-hospital stroke process of care
audits.setting: All acute-care hospitals in Catalonia; retrospective review of consecutive stroke admissions

cycle1.result: Eight performance measures achieved compliance >=75%, 4 of which were more than 90%; the remaining showed lower adherence.

audits.other_findings: Care was heterogeneous across hospital levels; rehabilitation-related measures showed poor compliance compared with acute care measures. Global interobserver agreement was 0.7.

audits.title: The Stroke Practice Improvement Network: a quasiexperimental trial of a multifaceted intervention to improve quality.
audits.standard: Inhospital stroke performance measures: door to needle <1 hour, dysphagia screening, DVT prophylaxis, warfarin for atrial fibrillation
audits.setting: 13 hospitals (Stroke Practice Improvement Network), neurology departments

cycle1.result: Preintervention data on 2071 patients; adherence figures not reported in abstract.

audits.intervention: Audit feedback alone versus audit feedback plus site-specific interventions (standing orders, standardised dysphagia screens) over 6 months.

cycle2.result: Improved adherence for only one of 3 measures: atrial fibrillation warfarin 98% v 87% in intervention vs control.

audits.other_findings: Site-specific interventions were imperfectly implemented in the 6-month period.
audits.citation: Hinchey JA, Shephard T, Tonn ST, Ruthazer R, Hermann RC, Selker HP, et al.. The Stroke Practice Improvement Network: a quasiexperimental trial of a multifaceted intervention to improve quality. audits.title: The Second Stroke Audit of Catalonia shows improvements in many, but not all quality indicators.
audits.standard: 13 evidence-based stroke performance measures (Catalan stroke guidelines)
audits.setting: 47 acute hospitals, Catalonia

cycle1.result: tPA 2.8%; stroke unit admission 16.6%; seven-day mortality 9.5%.

audits.intervention: Delivery of stroke guidelines between audits.

cycle2.result: tPA 5.9%; stroke unit admission 22.6%; seven-day mortality 6.8%; seven measures improved.

audits.other_findings: Management of hypertension, dyslipidaemia and antithrombotics at discharge worsened; three measures unchanged.

audits.standard: Stroke care from prevention to long-term care
audits.setting: Hospitals, general practices, community services and nursing homes in the Republic of Ireland

audits.title: Retrospective audit of the acute management of stroke in two district general hospitals in the uk.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians (London) stroke guidelines; audit targets 70%
audits.setting: Two district general hospitals in the same trust (Derby)

cycle1.result: Most CT head imaging done after 24 hours; low carotid ultrasound referral; warfarin underused in AF; TIA patients mostly not followed up by stroke specialists.

audits.other_findings: Occupational therapy and psychological assessment were omitted in most patients; dysphagia and physiotherapy assessments delayed.

audits.title: Variations in acute hospital stroke care and factors influencing adherence to quality indicators in 6 European audits.
audits.standard: Predefined acute stroke care quality indicators (thrombolysis, anticoagulation, stroke unit care, dysphagia testing, antiplatelets)
audits.setting: Six national/regional stroke audits (Germany, Poland, Scotland, Catalonia, Sweden, England/Wales/Northern Ireland) in the European Implementation Score collaboration

cycle1.result: Substantial variation in adherence to quality indicators; older age associated with lower probability of thrombolysis, anticoagulation or stroke unit care and higher probability of dysphagia testing; women less likely to receive anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy or stroke unit care.

audits.other_findings: No major weekend effect was found.
audits.citation: Wiedmann S, Hillmann S, Abilleira S, Dennis M, Hermanek P, Niewada M, et al.. Variations in acute hospital stroke care and factors influencing adherence to quality indicators in 6 European audits. Stroke. 2015;46(2):579-581. doi:10.1161/strokeaha.114.007504. PMID: 25550369.

audits.title: [Auditing as a tool for ongoing improvement in the Stroke Care Plan of the Region of Aragon].
audits.standard: 48 quality indicators selected for scientific evidence or clinical relevance
audits.setting: General hospitals of the Aragonese Health Service

cycle1.result: Baseline audit of 48 indicators (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Implementation of the Aragon Stroke Care Plan (PAIA), with generalisation of specialised care and creation of stroke units.

cycle2.result: 31 indicators improved significantly (including medical record quality, neurological assessment, initial preventive measures and swallowing test), 2 declined and 15 did not change.

audits.other_findings: An intermediate audit was done in 2010 (340 cases); the two indicators that declined related to rehabilitation.

audits.title: Multicenter, Prospective, Controlled, Before-and-After, Quality Improvement Study (Stroke123) of Acute Stroke Care.
audits.standard: Stroke clinical care quality indicators (composite of up to 8 indicators; 4 national indicators)
audits.setting: 19 hospitals in Queensland vs 23 other Australian hospitals

cycle1.result: Baseline audit and feedback phase.

audits.intervention: Financial incentives (21 months) then externally facilitated QI workshops with action plans (9 months).

cycle2.result: 18% improvement in median composite score; 14% after financial incentives; 8% for action plan indicators; national score improved 17% vs 0% in other hospitals.

audits.other_findings: Access to stroke units improved more in Queensland than elsewhere.
audits.citation: Cadilhac DA, Grimley R, Kilkenny MF, Andrew NE, Lannin NA, Hill K, et al.. Multicenter, Prospective, Controlled, Before-and-After, Quality Improvement Study (Stroke123) of Acute Stroke Care. Stroke. 2019;50(6):1525-1530. doi:10.1161/strokeaha.118.023075. PMID: 31084337.

audits.title: Quality and Outcomes of Acute Stroke Care for People With and Without Aphasia.
audits.standard: Quality of care indicators aligned with national evidence-based stroke guidelines
audits.setting: Australian acute hospitals, Stroke Foundation National Stroke Audit (2017, 2019, 2021)

cycle1.result: Patients with aphasia less often assessed for mood (23% vs 30%), given risk factor education (59% vs 70%) or involved in care planning (83% vs 95%).

audits.other_findings: 3122 (26.9%) had aphasia; they had more complications (aOR 1.46) and in-hospital deaths (aOR 2.86).
audits.citation: Stone M, Wallace SJ, Copland DA, Cadilhac DA, Hill K, Purvis T, et al.. Quality and Outcomes of Acute Stroke Care for People With and Without Aphasia. Arch Phys Med Rehabil. 2026;107(2):188-197. doi:10.1016/j.apmr.2025.07.007. PMID: 40685004.
